question:
A customer reports a defect in the executable we shipped to them two years ago, and to investigate it we need that very same executable back, byte for byte, but the toolchain and third-party libraries on our machines have been upgraded since then. What should the team have been tracking and preserving so that this would be possible?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

To reproduce a shipped executable byte-for-byte after toolchain upgrades, teams must place all relevant artifacts—source code, build tools (compilers, etc.), build instructions, third-party libraries, configuration data, and release documentation—under SCM control and preserve them in a software library with version and baseline tracking.

# Guidelines

- Place supporting tools (e.g., compilers) and associated build instructions under SCM control so that the correct versions are available [SWEBOK excerpt b4b4c90248f42cd3ae78] software configuration item. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt e082f1c815b2042b56a6].")

- Ensure SCM can [SWEBOK excerpt af43ae3c37d081b1c9b8], using the software library as a key element. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt ed245abb0f39c360af98].")

- Identify and control all software items that may become SCIs, including source and executable code, software tools, testing materials, plans, specifications, design documentation, and data. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management and Change Control/Software Configuration Items Selection and Change Recording.md)

- Use version control tools to [SWEBOK excerpt bcd2d492981cc51e057c], and maintain a repository that stores binaries created during the build process. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Configuration Management System Tools and Components.md)

- Establish baseline identification so that specific versions of all configuration items are captured at points of stability, enabling later reconstruction of exact product states. (source: "Baselines are identified where stability is intended.")

- Include [SWEBOK excerpt b193be691c4244a432a8] in SCM planning, considering [SWEBOK excerpt 302a3cac0e83930b5763] [SWEBOK excerpt 065a50459d05a95509d4]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Interface Control/SCM Workbenches and Vendor Control Planning.md)

- Preserve build process outputs as records, since [SWEBOK excerpt 626e98b737e85a1b3bcb] and [SWEBOK excerpt becf65fa53345037f81a]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Build Quality Assurance and Configuration Management/Build Process Quality Verification and Documentation.md)

- Document release contents in a version description document (VDD) that identifies the physical contents of each release, including which product items were delivered and which variants were selected. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 1bc7457ba6b688fca089]).")

- Track which approved software change requests ([SWEBOK excerpt fd0449d3e6272a97c9f3], so the exact composition of any shipped version is known. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Change Management and Version Control/Implementing Software Changes and Tracking.md)

- Include [SWEBOK excerpt c4e1be1200adcea889ba]—and SCM schedules in the SCM plan so that the infrastructure for preserving artifacts is maintained throughout the software life cycle. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Plan Development.md)
